old_caption: The video showcases a Sony 5 CD Changer Disc Exchange System placed on a flat surface. The device is black with a digital display panel featuring buttons for various functions such as play, stop, pause, and track selection. A hand appears, placing two CDs into the changer: one yellow with "ATLANTIC" written on it and another disc with purple and red sections. The tray remains open throughout the sequence. The background includes a piece of paper and a teal-colored object, possibly packaging or a bag, resting on the surface behind the device. The focus remains on the CD changer throughout the sequence, highlighting its operation and functionality.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a Sony 5 CD Changer Disc Exchange System placed on a flat surface. The device is black with a digital display panel featuring buttons for various functions such as play, stop, pause, and track selection. A hand appears, placing two CDs into the changer: one yellow with "ATLANTIC" written on it and another red with "Captain Fantastic" visible. The hand then closes the tray, and the changer begins to rotate the discs, indicating the start of the disc exchange process. The background includes a piece of paper and a teal-colored object, possibly packaging or a bag, resting on the surface behind the device. The focus remains on the CD changer throughout the sequence, highlighting its operation and functionality.
caption: The video showcases a black Sony five-disc CD changer resting on a dark surface with its disc tray extended, a yellow-and-black 'ATLANTIC' disc already seated in the left pocket and the right pocket empty, while a white sheet and a teal object sit behind the unit and the front LCD displays track and time readouts. A hand holding a red-and-purple 'Captain Fantastic' disc enters from the right edge and moves the disc leftward and downward over the vacant pocket. The fingers lower it into the right recess and press gently to seat it flat. As the placement proceeds, the LCD time advances through several increments. The hand then releases the disc and withdraws rightward out of the tray area. With the hand gone, both discs occupy the left and right pockets while the tray remains open.
